title: Over 30 dead, hundreds missing in Nepal floods; India rushes relief material
content: A massive flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district has caused widespread damage and claimed seventeen lives. Over one hundred Indian nationals are reported missing after the sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River. Many missing individuals are believed to be pilgrims traveling to Tibet for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. Rescue operations are underway with helicopters and drones searching for the missing people.

title: India vs Sri Lanka: A hold, the choke and then the frustrating close
content: India endured a frustrating day in Colombo, allowing Sri Lanka's Pasindu Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis to dictate terms before three late wickets gave the visitors a foothold. With rain cutting the day short, Sonal Dinusha remains the last major hurdle between India and a series clean sweep.

title: In 1984, NASA sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
content: Thousands of honeybees traveled into space aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery in 1984.  These bees were sent to microgravity to see if they could survive and build their famous honeycomb.  Initially, some bees crashed into walls, but they adapted within days.  By the mission's end, the bees flew normally and built about 200 cm of honeycomb.  Most bees survived, and the queen laid eggs which did not hatch after returning.

title: 'Very rarely do I get chance to play red-ball cricket': Arshdeep
content: India pacer Arshdeep Singh used the Duleep Trophy to prove his readiness for Test cricket after a long gap from red-ball cricket. He took four wickets in North Zone’s 52-run win over West Zone and said he had specifically trained with the red ball. Arshdeep also stressed the value of patience, tactical bowling and domestic cricket in preparing for Tests.

title: GPS can't work everywhere, so scientists test navigation using cosmic rays
content: Japanese scientists are testing a new navigation system using cosmic ray muons. This system can work in places where GPS signals are unavailable, like underground. Muons can penetrate dense materials, which GPS signals cannot do effectively. Researchers have demonstrated this technology's potential for guiding robots and vehicles. The technology is still under development and requires further refinement for widespread use.

title: 2nd Test: Rain delays India’s impending series victory over Sri Lanka
content: Sri Lanka ended day four of the second Test at 229 for six after India’s bowlers struck late. Pasindu Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis led the fightback with a 115-run stand, while Sonal Dinusha scored 103 earlier. India’s late wickets put them in control, but rain and bad light halted play, leaving Sri Lanka fighting to avoid defeat on day five.

title: Grand Teton ranch sold in 1967 stayed with same family for 39 more years
content: The 4 Lazy F Ranch in Wyoming remained with the Frew family for decades after they bought it in 1927. Emily Frew Oliver turned the family summer retreat into a dude ranch in 1950. In 1967, she sold the property to the federal government but kept a life estate. She voluntarily gave it up in 2006, ending her family’s long connection with the historic ranch.

title: IBM built a secret NSA computer in 1962 that ran 200x faster; how a worn part ended it
content: The year 1962 marked the inception of a clandestine project by IBM for the NSA, giving rise to the secret computer named Harvest. For fourteen years, this remarkable machine tackled critical cryptographic computations during the tense Cold War era, boasting speeds that eclipsed its peers by a factor of 200.

title: How Hegseth's 'purge' triggered a US Army leadership crisis as Iran war nears six months
content: The US Army faces a leadership void with no permanent chief of staff.  Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has removed several senior officers, impacting leadership continuity.  This occurs while American bases in West Asia endure drone and missile attacks.  The Army's senior civilian official is also expected to depart soon.  This significant personnel churn raises concerns about institutional expertise and decision-making.

content: The Australia fast bowler took 10 wickets in the match, including 6/12 in the first innings and 4/39 in the second, helping Australia register an innings and 51-run win and level the World Test Championship series.

title: Karishma Tanna shares postpartum routine; reveals what she eats and drinks
content: In an inspiring revelation, actress Karishma Tanna opened up about her postpartum care routine following the birth of her son on July 29, 2026. She emphasized the importance of nourishing foods and drinks to enhance milk production, while also sharing effective remedies for common postpartum issues like back pain and nipple soreness. Staying well-hydrated and regularly using a belly support belt were key components of her recovery.

title: Cash buyers dominated the US housing boom. Now financed buyers are fighting back
content: Cash purchases in the US housing market are decreasing significantly.  This trend emerges as home sales slow and inventory levels rise.  Price growth has also moderated considerably, benefiting financed buyers.  Financed buyers are now winning competitive bidding situations more frequently.  Cash buyers are becoming less dominant as the market stabilizes.

title: Villages washed away as massive flash floods tear through Nepal - watch
content: A sudden cloudburst triggered severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi River, devastating Nepal's Rasuwa district. Tragically, at least eight people have lost their lives, and several others remain unaccounted for. The disaster has wreaked havoc on local markets, roads, and bridges. Rescue teams are in full swing, employing helicopters from the Nepal army. Authorities are urging residents living near riverbanks in multiple districts to remain vigilant and prepared.

title: Builder told to pay Rs 6 cr to housing society over delay in occupation certificate
content: A Mumbai builder must pay Rs 6 crore to a housing society. This payment is for failing to secure an occupation certificate for over twenty years. Members faced demolition risk and lived without essential services. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered the builder to rectify this. The builder must also obtain the occupation certificate within twelve months.

title: Former Premier League star Akos Buzsaky missing, Hungarian police search
content: Former Premier League footballer Akos Buzsaky is reportedly missing in Hungary. Police have been searching for the ex-Queens Park Rangers midfielder since August 18. His family is also actively trying to locate the 44-year-old former player. Buzsaky has spent considerable time working as a construction contractor in Greece. Hungarian authorities have not released further details regarding his disappearance.

title: 'Played competitive matches against boys': Pak skipper reveals Asia Cup prep
content: Pakistan’s women’s cricket team played full T20 matches against a men’s side during their pre-Asia Cup camp in Lahore to prepare for pressure situations. Captain Fatima Sana believes the unusual training will improve decision-making and composure. Pakistan, who have never won the Women’s Asia Cup, begin their campaign against Thailand on September 1 and face India on September 5.

title: Explained: When it makes sense to take a joint home loan and when it doesn’t
content: When two earning members of a household apply together for a loan, their combined income can potentially improve loan eligibility and help manage repayment burden more efficiently. Most banks and HFCs reiterate that adding an earning family member as a co-applicant can improve their borrowing eligibility.

title: A fatal pact, death note and poison: How a rifle coach came to haunt Andhra family

Her son survived the incident after being rescued from the river. The coach was arrested in Meerut after a special investigation team was formed. Police are investigating allegations of murder, threats, and financial control.

title: Rs 30 lakh a month for an intern? India’s trading firms are in a fierce talent war
content: In a bid to attract the brightest minds, high-frequency trading firms in India are ramping up intern compensation to unprecedented levels. This surge in hiring is influenced by stricter regulations on derivatives and a lull in equity market movements. Companies such as Quadeye and Graviton Research Capital are notably enhancing their internship packages, with global firms following suit to secure top quantitative talent from leading institutions.

title: ‘Toxic’ BO day 1 : Yash, Nayanthara, and Kiara Advani starrer gets strong start
content: Yash's new film 'Toxic' has achieved a significant opening day collection across India.  The action drama directed by Geetu Mohandas earned over forty-one crore rupees net.  Audience reactions are divided, praising visuals and Yash's presence but questioning the screenplay.  The Hindi version contributed the most to the film's opening day earnings.  'Toxic' now faces the weekend to sustain its box-office momentum.

title: How do navies hunt submarines? NATO's deadly game of detection beneath the waves
content: NATO navies are focusing on submarine detection and neutralization challenges.  Exercises like Northern Viking 26 highlight coordinated anti-submarine warfare efforts.  Modern warfare relies on advanced acoustic technology and persistent coordination between assets.  India is the only nation to sink a submerged submarine since World War Two.  Submarine and anti-submarine systems continue to advance, making submarine kills more difficult.

title: Dolly Parton walked so Taylor Swift could run
content: Dolly Parton’s impact transcends the realm of country music, leaving a mark on various genres and artists alike. Her prowess in songwriting and strategic business moves, particularly in managing her own intellectual property, showcases her talent. The exaggerated persona she cultivated enabled a blend of femininity with authority, influencing the likes of Taylor Swift and Beyoncé in their careers.

title: ‘Shouldn't it begin with Congress?' BJP targets Rahul over 'smash patriarchy’ remark

BJP leader Bansuri Swaraj accused Gandhi of hypocrisy and lacking a positive agenda.  She cited past Congress remarks against Kangana Ranaut and Hema Malini as examples.  Gandhi's campaign focused on challenging patriarchal systems and empowering women's choices.  He advocated for ending restrictions placed on women in Indian society.

title: India’s 1st hydrogen train travels 6,000 km; cuts 36,444 kg CO2 emissions
content: India’s first hydrogen train consists of 10 coaches and can accommodate 2,600 passengers. It operates between Jind and Sonipat in Haryana with a maximum operating speed of 75 kmph, although the train has been designed to reach 110 kmph.

title: Why India’s rice exports to Iran may survive Trump's sanctions threat
content: India's rice exports to Iran are expected to continue despite tougher US sanctions.  Demand from Iran remains firm for food security reasons, ensuring continued purchases.  Indian exporters utilize alternative payment channels in countries like Turkey and the UAE.  Essential goods like rice and pharmaceuticals are unlikely to face disruption.  Bilateral trade has significantly declined from its previous peak levels.

title: Watch: Gangajal in hand, UP councillors 'swear oath' to share bribes equally
content: A video shows Shahjahanpur Municipal Corporation councillors taking an oath to share civic funds. The purported oath states all income would be divided equally among sixty councillors. This viral video has prompted the civic body to order an official inquiry. The inquiry will investigate the authenticity of the video and its participants. Further action will be taken based on the inquiry's findings.

title: ‘Be ready for cockroaches!’ CJP renews Sept 5 protest call over 3 pending demands

The party seeks compensation and withdrawal of FIRs against student protesters.  Assurances were given by ministers after talks on July 25.  The march will proceed from India Gate to the Police Headquarters.

title: Kelli Finglass opens up on possibly leaving Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders
content: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' Kelli Finglass opens up about her 35-season journey, social media criticism and the changing meaning of leadership. Reflecting on her career, she says vulnerability has become more powerful than perfection, especially as television has allowed audiences to see the women beyond their performances. Finglass also acknowledges that retirement could eventually become a personal decision, with family and the possibility of becoming a grandmother potentially guiding her toward a new chapter.

title: Bella Mir suffers first MMA loss to Alex Apodaca in historic DWCS upset
content: Alex Apodaca shocked DWCS Week 3 by beating Bella Mir, the night’s -6000 favorite, by unanimous decision. All three judges scored the fight 29-28 for Apodaca, who improved to 8-1 and secured a UFC contract. Mir suffered the first professional MMA loss of her career, falling to 3-1. The result became the biggest upset in Dana White’s Contender Series history, while four other fighters also earned UFC contracts that night.

title: HAL, Safran seal engine deal to power multi-role choppers
content: HAL and Safran Helicopter Engines signed a contract for the Aravalli engine. This new engine will power India's proposed 13-tonne multi-role helicopter. The agreement covers design, development, manufacture, and lifecycle support. This collaboration marks a significant step towards self-reliance in aero-engine technologies. The Aravalli engine will also find applications in civil aviation missions.

title: How a family reunion in China ended in a 3-year prison term for artist Gao Zhen
content: Chinese artist Gao Zhen received a three-year prison sentence for his satirical artwork.  Authorities charged him with "infringing upon the reputation of heroes" for his art.  Gao's wife expressed deep disappointment and sadness over the unexpected conviction.  His supporters argue the artworks predate the law under which he was prosecuted.  The sentence highlights China's narrowing space for artistic and political expression.

title: Chennai Canvas: Madras Week Episode 4 | How cinema became part of Chennai
content: Cinema is woven into the fabric of Chennai’s cultural memory. From romance, longing and movie-inspired moments on the city’s beaches to the dramatic shift from celluloid reels to digital projection, Chennai’s relationship with the big screen has constantly evolved. At the heart of that journey are theatres that became landmarks in their own right, including Royapettah’s Pilot Theatre. Episode 4 of Chennai Canvas, for Madras Week, revisits these spaces, memories and technological changes to explore why, for generations of Chennai residents, the city and cinema have been inseparable.
